extraction_warnings: This paper primarily reports study-level/aggregate data for the Yanomami/Brazil cohort (n=15); per-subject demographic and sample metadata (age, sex, sample IDs) are stated to be in Supplementary Table 1, which was not provided in the input text.
The schema fields (subject_id, sample_id, age, sex, etc.) are typically sample-level but could not be populated at that granularity due to lack of per-sample data in the provided text.

Comparator cohorts (Yanomami/Venezuela, Matses, Tunapuco, US) are secondary/reanalyzed datasets from other publications (Clemente et al. 2015; Obregon-Tito et al. 2015; HMP Consortium 2012) and were not treated as primary subgroups for this extraction, since the schema targets the study's own generated samples.
control and target_condition fields do not clearly apply as this is a descriptive microbiome characterization study rather than a case-control disease study; marked not_reported.

This paper focuses on gut microbiome taxonomic/functional characterization of hunter-gatherer groups; none of the schema's clinical/demographic/disease fields (age, BMI, disease status, treatment, tumor staging, etc.) are explicitly reported in the main text for individual participants.
Participant age and gender data are stated to be summarized in Supplementary Table 1, which is not included in the provided text, so exact values could not be extracted.

The 'disease' field inference (possible 'Healthy' status) is based on a general population-level statement about absence of chronic diseases among Yanomami, not a direct clinical assessment of study participants; treated as low-confidence inferred but ultimately reported as not_reported to avoid fabrication.

biomarker_unit and biomarker_value fields could not be populated with specific numeric values as the paper only shows LDA scores graphically (Figure 3C) without reporting exact per-genus values in text.
